mobile.label: 1 · Карточка на подставке
mobile.prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Produce one polished full-screen MOBILE Japanese vocabulary-learning app visual target, portrait 960x2080, approximately a 390x844 CSS pixel phone viewport. No phone bezel or comparison montage. This is a design study; show one entire usable screen. Reference images preserve the approved cozy illustrated visual world, warm golden wood, detailed soft 2D painting and the cream cat with sage scarf. Use refined Japanese mincho typography for the kanji, elegant readable Cyrillic book typography for Russian, restrained dark-brown ink on warm light paper. At phone scale Russian answer labels should look about 20-22px, question about 22px, reading 22px, kanji about 100px; all controls at least 48px high with generous gaps. Leave safe space at top and bottom. Small understated header with 'まるごと', a back action 'Словарь', and progress '1 / 4'. The exact task is 'Как переводится слово?' with kanji '魚' and reading 'さかな' above it. Four choices, exact text: 'мясо', 'пить', 'рыба', 'Токио'. No fish illustration or other clue revealing the answer. All text baselines perfectly horizontal. ALL answer elements front-facing, axis-aligned, with straight horizontal edges, zero perspective, zero rotation, NO trapezoidal or angled answer panels. Make the text easy to read first. The cat is a small companion, about 80-90 CSS pixels wide, in spare space near the lower edge, never covering answers. No huge empty panels, no gray filled rectangles, no generic rounded dashboard buttons, no colored stripes or divider rules, no decorative badges, no XP, no childish doodles, no black outlines, no stock mobile UI kit. Material quality and typography should belong with the approved background and cat. Do not overcrowd or shrink the task to fit decoration. Direction 1: frontal desk view. Reference image 1 is the approved portrait room and should remain recognizably that room/garden, softly visible above the wooden desktop. Reference image 3 is the new desktop stationery study: carry over its beautifully illustrated thick washi card, delicate botanical corner detail and subtle brass support. Recompose for the phone rather than scaling down the desktop screenshot. Put a compact frontal paper card in the upper-middle, about 85% of screen width, with comfortable text margins. Below it, four beautifully textured paper answer slips in a perfectly straight two-by-two grid. The slips may have natural fibrous edges and contact shadows, but their type and outer silhouette must be level and unforeshortened, equally sized. Keep some room below for the small original cat. The UI has the tactile polish of a carefully illustrated game, not a faux-parchment HTML panel.
